text:
Dana Lo: sanity check on checklist copy for the “Rate limits & quotas” step. Right now it says “If you hit a 429, you exceeded your quota.” That’s not always true, right?

Ibrahim Khan: yeah 429 is overloaded atm. Can be burst rate limiting, can be quota cap, can be concurrency. We should be precise or we’ll create more tickets.

Wei Chen: +1. Docs draft currently: “429 means you sent too many requests.” But people ask “too many compared to what?” and “why did my first request 429?”

Cole Summers: correct: we return 429 for (a) rate limit buckets (req/min + tokens/min) and (b) hard quota caps (monthly token budget) when enabled. Different error codes though.

Dana Lo: do we actually include an error code consistently?

Amara Diallo: gateway side: response body includes `error.code` in all 429 paths we control.
- `rate_limit_exceeded` when you exceeded a time-window bucket (req/min, tokens/min)
- `quota_exceeded` when you’re out of purchased/allocated quota (monthly)
- `concurrency_limit_exceeded` when you have too many in-flight requests for the project

Amara Diallo: headers:
- `retry-after` is set for `rate_limit_exceeded` and sometimes for concurrency (best effort)
- `x-request-id` always
- `x-rw-ratelimit-limit-requests` / `x-rw-ratelimit-remaining-requests` / `x-rw-ratelimit-reset-requests` (same set for tokens) are only on rate-limit bucket 429s

Priya Shah: from Support: most confusion is “I’m on free trial and got 429 after like 3 calls” -> usually they were streaming and token/min got burned, or they had a tight default limit on a brand new org. Also some folks loop on retry w/out backoff.

Nikhil Sharma: for checklist step, we should keep it understandable for new users. But we can link to a deeper doc section that enumerates the types + headers.

Wei Chen: what should the checklist microcopy say, then?

Ibrahim Khan: proposal for step description:
“Learn what triggers 429s (rate limits, token limits, and concurrency caps) and how to handle them with backoff using `Retry-After`.”
Then add a one-liner note: “Quota exhaustion returns 429 with `error.code=quota_exceeded`.”

Dana Lo: does “quota exhaustion” mean monthly? Or also “project limit”?

Cole Summers: we use “quota” for the monthly budget. The per-minute buckets are “rate limits.” There’s also a project-level “max concurrency” setting that behaves like a limit, not quota.

Monica Patel: +1 to that terminology. In SDK guides we’re trying to standardize:
- Rate limits = time-window (req/min, tokens/min)
- Quota = monthly budget
- Concurrency limit = in-flight cap

Amara Diallo: also: we should avoid saying “429 == too many requests” only. Sometimes it’s “too many tokens” and customers interpret that as “my prompt is too large” (that’s 400/413 depending).

Wei Chen: ok, updated copy idea (for checklist card):
Title: “Handle rate limits (429) & quotas”
Body: “429 can mean you hit a rate limit (requests/tokens per minute) or a concurrency cap. If you’re out of monthly quota, 429 returns with `error.code=quota_exceeded`. Use exponential backoff and respect `Retry-After`.”
CTA: “Read how rate limits & quotas work” (deep link)

Nikhil Sharma: this feels good. Maybe remove some jargon from the body but keep the `quota_exceeded` bit since it’s actionable.

Priya Shah: pls keep “tokens per minute” explicitly. That’s the #1 “surprise” during onboarding, esp with streaming.

Dana Lo: should we call out that parallel streaming requests count towards concurrency? got a ticket where they opened 20 streams.

Amara Diallo: yes, each streaming response counts as 1 in-flight until closed. That’s why concurrency 429s look “random” in dev.

Ibrahim Khan: could add a short bullet in the linked doc, not in the checklist card. The card should stay scannable.

Monica Patel: decision:
- Checklist microcopy: keep simple but accurate; mention req/min + tokens/min + concurrency; mention `Retry-After`; mention quota returns `quota_exceeded`.
- Docs page: add a table “429 types” with: `error.code`, common causes, headers, recommended client behavior.
Wei — can you update the docs snippet and I’ll sync it with SDK retry guidance?

Wei Chen: yup. I’ll update the troubleshooting section too (“Why am I getting 429?”) with the three cases + headers.

Cole Summers: I’ll drop exact naming for the headers + example response payload in the doc draft so it matches reality.

Dana Lo: awesome. I’ll update the checklist copy ticket with the approved wording + the “don’t say quota == 429 always” note.

Nikhil Sharma: thanks all. this should reduce SUP-9182 style confusion.

Monica Patel: :thumbsup: once merged, we should make sure Console step links to the new anchor (rate-limit-429) and not the generic quotas page.
